name: Myeloid Sarcoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues

criteria.description: Presence of extramedullary tumor composed of immature myeloid cells confirmed by histopathology
Immunohistochemical staining positive for myeloid markers such as myeloperoxidase (MPO), CD33, CD68
Bone marrow examination to assess for concurrent or antecedent acute myeloid leukemia or other myeloid neoplasms

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathologic confirmation of extramedullary immature myeloid cell tumor with positive myeloid immunophenotyping
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may be challenging without concurrent bone marrow involvement; molecular studies can aid diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Palpable extramedullary tumor mass composed of immature myeloid cells
pathognomonic.notes: Typically firm, localized mass often greenish due to myeloperoxidase content
searchTerms: palpable tumor of immature blood cells

pathognomonic.notes: Greenish hue caused by high myeloperoxidase enzyme concentration

common.symptomName: Localized swelling or mass effect symptoms
common.notes: May cause pain or functional impairment depending on site

searchTerms: fever related to whole body condition
lymph node swelling close to tumor

occasional.symptomName: Neurological deficits due to central nervous system involvement
occasional.notes: Occurs if tumor invades CNS structures
searchTerms: nerve deficits related to central nervous system

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory symptoms from thoracic mass effect
searchTerms: respiratory symptoms due to thoracic tumor
shortness of breath from chest swelling

occasional.symptomName: Gastrointestinal obstruction symptoms if abdominal involvement

rare.symptomName: Ophthalmological involvement causing proptosis or visual disturbance
Renal impairment secondary to tumor infiltration
Cardiovascular compromise due to mediastinal mass
searchTerms: heart or vessel problems from chest mass
cardiovascular issues due to mediastinal tumor
blood flow compromise from chest swelling

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear may show circulating myeloblasts
imaging: CT or MRI showing localized soft tissue mass
PET scan demonstrating hypermetabolic extramedullary lesions
genetic: Cytogenetic abnormalities common in AML such as t(8;21), inv(16), or 11q23 rearrangements
Molecular mutations including FLT3, NPM1 may be present
other: Histopathology showing sheets of immature myeloid cells
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD33, CD68, MPO

distinguishingFeatures: Lymphoma cells express lymphoid markers (CD20, CD3) unlike myeloid sarcoma
Different immunophenotypic profile with absence of myeloid markers

redFlags: Signs of acute leukemia or bone marrow failure
references: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues, 2017
Pileri SA et al. Myeloid sarcoma: clinico-pathologic, phenotypic and cytogenetic analysis of 92 adult patients. Leukemia. 2007
Kaur P et al. Myeloid sarcoma: a clinical review. J Hematol Oncol. 2020
